Question: Define \(x\heartsuit y\) to be \(|x - y|\) for all real numbers \(x\) and \(y.\) Which of the following statements is not true?

Choices.A: \(x\heartsuit y = y\heartsuit x\) for all \(x\) and \(y\)

Solution:
The operation gives \(x\heartsuit0=|x|\). Since absolute value is never negative, this cannot equal a negative \(x\). For example,
\[
(-1)\heartsuit0=|-1|=1\ne-1.
\]
This disproves statement C, which claims equality for every real \(x\).

The remaining statements all hold. Swapping \(x\) and \(y\) changes the difference only by sign, so \(|x-y|=|y-x|\), proving A. Multiplying a number by \(2\) doubles its absolute value, so
\[
|2x-2y|=2|x-y|,
\]
proving B. Also, \(|x-x|=0\), proving D. Finally, if \(x\ne y\), their difference is nonzero and its absolute value is strictly positive, proving E.

Therefore the statement that is not true is \(\boxed{\mathrm{C}}\).
